correctness.rationale: Assuming the explicitly credited Homma--Kim criterion (a plane-filling degree q+2 equation F_A is smooth over algebraic closure iff its representing 3x3 matrix has irreducible cubic characteristic polynomial), reconstructed the argument. Trace of scalar I in characteristic 3 is zero, so trace descends to W_q; on trace-zero space Q(A)=tr(A^2)/2 is unchanged by scalar addition. If tr A=0 and t^3+c t+d is irreducible, the additive map t->t^3+c t cannot be bijective, so its nonzero kernel element yields -c=Q(A) a nonzero square. Any binary quadratic over odd F_q either has a nonzero zero or (if anisotropic) is a scalar norm from F_q^2 and takes every nonzero field value. Thus a two-plane of all-smooth equations cannot lie inside ker tr. Every all-smooth 2-plane has one-dimensional trace kernel. For any smooth A, K=F_q[A] is degree-three field; taking B outside span{I,A} gives two-dimensional non-scalar span with all nonzero members of irreducible degree three, hence smooth; this covers every r>=1 and preserves rational-member, not geometrically all-member, scope. Independent GF3 field-multiplication witness/trace calculation supports the structural proof. Literature matrix criterion itself is an attributed premise, not verified from its inaccessible full text.

broader_coverage.reasoning: General Chevalley-type determinant arguments can preclude 3-dimensional all-invertible matrix systems; that broadly covers the bare no-net numerical bound. They do not characterize the unique trace-zero intersection for every smooth pencil or guarantee field-generated pencils through every smooth curve, the separately motivated finer assertions.

originality.rationale: A bare no-smooth-net bound is not independently original: the cubic determinant and general finite-field polynomial zero principles provide broader restrictions on high-dimensional nonsingular matrix pencils. Originality is assessed on the additional characteristic-three structural assertion that each admissible smooth pencil has exactly one canonical trace-zero member, together with the every-smooth-member extension. These assertions do not follow from Asgarli--Ghioca general existence nor from the Homma--Kim individual-curve smoothness statement alone without the additional quadratic norm argument. No identified Resultary prior theorem establishes both for all F_{3^r}. This is best-of-knowledge; an inaccessible relevant matrix-space paper could subsume the finer result.

value.rationale: The trace-zero selector provides a projectively natural marked rational member of every smooth minimum-degree plane-filling pencil, and the extension theorem shows these pencils exist through all smooth members in every characteristic-three extension field. This is a meaningful classification/obstruction of a geometrically motivated moduli problem, not merely a q=3 enumeration. Value is attributed to these finer structural statements, not to generic no-net dimension counting alone.

limitations: Only minimum degree q+2 plane-filling forms in characteristic 3; pencils need only rational members to be smooth. The no-net number alone is not treated as independently valuable novelty; geometric members over extensions can be singular.
